stem: A 58-year-old has taken tamoxifen for 3 years after breast cancer. She mentions light vaginal spotting for 2 weeks and wonders whether to wait until her next annual visit. What is the best response?
correct: Arrange prompt gynecologic evaluation for endometrial disease

distractors.text: Reassure her; spotting is expected and needs no workup
distractors.why: Bleeding on tamoxifen should not be dismissed.

distractors.text: Switch to raloxifene, which treats the endometrium
distractors.why: Raloxifene is endometrium-neutral; the bleeding still needs evaluation.

distractors.text: Add estradiol alone to stabilize the uterine lining
distractors.why: Unopposed estrogen adds endometrial risk.

distractors.text: Check hematocrit and PSA, then review in 6 months
distractors.why: Those are testosterone monitoring items.

why_correct: Tamoxifen is an antagonist in breast but an agonist in endometrium, raising the risk of hyperplasia and cancer. Abnormal bleeding needs prompt gynecologic evaluation.
takeaway: Bleeding on tamoxifen: evaluate now.
discriminator: Same drug, opposite action in two tissues.

stem: A 67-year-old with stable angina takes isosorbide mononitrate daily and asks for sildenafil. Which response matches the lecture?
correct: Do not prescribe; involve his cardiologist about the nitrate first

distractors.text: Prescribe sildenafil and space it 4 hours from the nitrate
distractors.why: Spacing is for alpha1 blockers; nitrates are an absolute contraindication.

distractors.text: Prescribe tadalafil instead, which is safe with nitrates
distractors.why: The whole class is contraindicated with nitrates.

distractors.text: Prescribe sildenafil at half dose with close monitoring
distractors.why: No dose makes the combination acceptable.

distractors.text: Stop the nitrate yourself today and start sildenafil
distractors.why: Any change to anginal therapy involves his cardiologist.

why_correct: Nitrates raise NO and cGMP; PDE5 inhibitors stop cGMP breakdown. Together: profound hypotension and syncope. It is an absolute contraindication, and ED treatment decisions involve the cardiologist.
takeaway: Nitrate on board: no PDE5 inhibitor.
discriminator: Absolute with nitrates; caution with alpha1 blockers.

stem: A 44-year-old premenopausal woman with estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer asks why she was not given anastrozole alone like her 68-year-old aunt. Which explanation is correct?
correct: Her ovaries still make estrogen, so it is not enough alone

distractors.text: Aromatase inhibitors only work when the uterus is absent
distractors.why: The issue is ovarian estrogen, not the uterus.

distractors.text: Aromatase inhibitors raise endometrial cancer risk before menopause
distractors.why: That risk belongs to tamoxifen.

distractors.text: Aromatase inhibitors need CYP2D6, which falls after menopause
distractors.why: CYP2D6 activation is the tamoxifen story.

distractors.text: Her bones are too strong for an aromatase inhibitor to act
distractors.why: Bone loss is an adverse effect, not a requirement.

why_correct: Aromatase inhibitors block peripheral estrogen synthesis. Before menopause the ovary still makes estrogen, so an aromatase inhibitor alone is insufficient.
takeaway: Aromatase inhibitors alone are for after menopause.
discriminator: Peripheral synthesis vs ovarian synthesis.

stem: A 68-year-old has taken dutasteride for 3 years. His PSA was 3.0 ng/mL before treatment and is 2.6 ng/mL now. How should the PA interpret this?

distractors.text: Reassuring: the PSA has fallen from 3.0 to 2.6
distractors.why: It should have fallen by about half.

distractors.text: Reassuring: 5-ARIs do not change PSA values
distractors.why: They lower PSA by roughly half.

distractors.text: Concerning: on a 5-ARI a PSA of 2.6 reads as about 1.3
distractors.why: The correction is to double, not halve.

distractors.text: Uninterpretable: PSA cannot be used on dutasteride
distractors.why: It can be used once adjusted.

why_correct: 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors lower PSA by roughly half with long-term therapy, so the value is read accordingly. A PSA that has barely fallen is effectively higher than baseline.
takeaway: On finasteride or dutasteride, double the PSA.
discriminator: Compare the adjusted value with baseline.

stem: A 38-year-old who smokes a pack a day asks for 'the regular pill' for contraception. Her mother had a pulmonary embolism at 45. Which option is most appropriate?
correct: A progestin-only method, because estrogen is contraindicated

distractors.text: A combined pill, because her VTE risk is only theoretical
distractors.why: Smoking, age over 35 and family VTE history move her to contraindicated.

distractors.text: A combined pill plus low-dose aspirin to offset clot risk
distractors.why: The lecture's answer is to avoid estrogen, not to offset it.

distractors.text: Estradiol alone, because the dose is lower than the pill
distractors.why: It is still estrogen, and unopposed with a uterus.

distractors.text: Raloxifene, because it avoids the endometrial cancer risk
distractors.why: It is not a contraceptive and carries VTE risk itself.

stem: A 59-year-old on sildenafil starts ketoconazole. After his next dose he has a pounding headache, marked flushing and a blue tint to his vision. What explains the stronger effects?
correct: Ketoconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and raises sildenafil levels

distractors.text: Ketoconazole induces CYP3A4 and lowers sildenafil levels
distractors.why: Lower levels would weaken the effects.

distractors.text: Ketoconazole donates NO and raises cGMP like a nitrate
distractors.why: It is not a nitrate.

distractors.text: Ketoconazole blocks alpha1 receptors in vessel walls
distractors.why: That is tamsulosin.

distractors.text: The blue vision shows an allergy unrelated to dose
distractors.why: Visual change is a known, dose-related PDE5 effect.

why_correct: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin) raise PDE5 inhibitor levels. Headache, flushing, dyspepsia and blue-tinged vision are the class adverse effects, more notable with sildenafil.
takeaway: CYP3A4 inhibitor + PDE5 inhibitor = exaggerated effects.
discriminator: Expected adverse effects, at a higher level.

stem: An 82-year-old with mild dementia on donepezil has urge incontinence. She also takes diphenhydramine nightly. Her blood pressure is well controlled. Which plan is best?
correct: Stop diphenhydramine and choose mirabegron over oxybutynin

distractors.text: Start oxybutynin; it has the least CNS effect in the class
distractors.why: Oxybutynin has the highest CNS anticholinergic burden.

distractors.text: Start solifenacin and continue diphenhydramine for sleep
distractors.why: Anticholinergic burden is cumulative across her drugs.

distractors.text: Start oxybutynin; donepezil will cancel its side effects
distractors.why: Donepezil opposes antimuscarinics; they work against each other.

distractors.text: Start tamsulosin to relax the bladder outlet instead
distractors.why: Her problem is storage, not outlet obstruction.

why_correct: Antimuscarinics cause confusion in older adults, and the burden adds up across drugs such as diphenhydramine. Oxybutynin carries the highest CNS burden; cholinesterase inhibitors oppose antimuscarinics. Mirabegron, a beta3 agonist, avoids this.
takeaway: Dementia + urge incontinence: avoid oxybutynin, cut other anticholinergics.
discriminator: Count the whole anticholinergic load.
